questions.prompt: Consequentialist theories hold that moral value depends on:
choices: A Only the agent’s bloodline.
B Consequences—especially for the amount of good produced.
C Ritual purity alone.
D Aesthetic style of the speech act.

questions.prompt: Jeremy Bentham is portrayed as someone who:
choices: A Practiced law for fifty years after Oxford.
B Devoted his life to moral, political, and legal reform (Oxford law at 19; Philosophical Radicals).
C Rejected all talk of happiness.
D Founded only the Austrian School.

questions.prompt: On the Bentham/Mill happiness scale, “zero” means:
choices: A Infinite bliss.
B The action has no effect on anyone’s happiness.
C Mandatory punishment.
D Only physical pain.

questions.prompt: Bentham’s “greatest happiness of the whole community” talk illustrates:
choices: A A satisficing-only ethos with no maximizing language.
B A maximizing conception—pursue the greatest happiness as the end.
C Rejection of utility.
D Pure virtue ethics without outcomes.

questions.prompt: Mill especially worries that pleasures differ in:
choices: A Only calorie count.
B Kind/quality—not all pleasures are equal.
C Currency denomination alone.
D Geographic longitude.
